framework called `fuzzsim`). Read these files FIRST to learn the conventions and APIs you must
build on:

  /workspace/requirements/aflpp.yaml          <- THE REQUIREMENT. Every concept listed must exist.
  /workspace/fuzzsim/afl_fuzzer.py            <- AFL core (AFLFuzzer, QueueEntry, ExecResult, Dictionary,
                                                 havoc_mutate, havoc_stage, _rand_below, _wr16/_wr32/_rd16/_rd32,
                                                 ARITH_MAX, HAVOC_CYCLES, HAVOC_CYCLES_INIT, HAVOC_MIN,
                                                 HAVOC_STACK_POW2, MAP_SIZE)
  /workspace/fuzzsim/aflfast_schedules.py     <- PowerSchedule enum, EnergyComputer, ScheduleInputs, SCHEDULE_ORDER
  /workspace/fuzzsim/aflfast_search.py        <- AFLFastFuzzer, PathFrequencyTracker (subclassing example)
  /workspace/fuzzsim/fairfuzz_mask.py         <- another subclassing example (overriding havoc_stage)
  /workspace/fuzzsim/mutation.py              <- INTERESTING_8/16/32 and basic operators
  /workspace/fuzzsim/experiments/afl_experiment.py   <- INITIAL_SEEDS, DICTIONARY, run_afl, SEED=42, MAX_EXECS=30000
  /workspace/fuzzsim/experiments/aflfast_experiment.py <- experiment style to copy
  /workspace/fuzzsim/targets/crashme.py       <- the target program (30 edges; 26 reachable => 86.7%)

HARD RULES
- Determinism: every random draw must come from a numpy.random.RandomState seeded from an explicit
  seed (42). No time, no global random, no set-iteration-order dependence in anything that affects output.
- Do NOT modify any existing file. Only create the new files you are told to create.
- Match the surrounding code style exactly: module docstring explaining the paper mechanism, typed
  signatures, `from __future__ import annotations`, short comments only where they add information,
  constants documented with #: comments.
- Python 3 + numpy only (no third-party deps beyond numpy).


PUBLIC API CONTRACT (both modules and the experiment must agree on these EXACT names):

fuzzsim/aflpp_custom_mutator.py
  MAX_FILE (int constant, e.g. 1 << 20)
  class CustomMutator                      # base class, the AFL++ afl-fuzz-mutator.c API
      name: str  (class attribute)
      __init__(self, seed: int = 42)
      init(self, seed: int) -> None
      describe(self) -> str
      fuzz_count(self, buf: bytes) -> int
      fuzz(self, buf: bytes, add_buf: Optional[bytes] = None, max_size: int = MAX_FILE) -> bytes
      havoc_mutation(self, buf: bytes, max_size: int = MAX_FILE) -> bytes
      havoc_mutation_probability(self) -> int          # 0..100
      post_process(self, buf: bytes) -> bytes
      init_trim(self, buf: bytes) -> int               # number of trim steps
      trim(self) -> bytes                              # current trim candidate
      post_trim(self, success: bool) -> int            # next step index
      trim_full(self, buf, oracle) -> bytes            # convenience: run the whole trim loop
      queue_new_entry(self, buf: bytes, coverage) -> None

  class MutatorRegistry
      __init__(self, rng: Optional[np.random.RandomState] = None, seed: int = 42)
      register(self, mutator: CustomMutator, weight: float = 1.0) -> None
      unregister(self, name: str) -> bool
      get(self, name: str) -> Optional[CustomMutator]
      names(self) -> List[str]
      weights(self) -> Dict[str, float]
      probabilities(self) -> Dict[str, float]          # weights normalised to sum 1
      select(self, rng=None) -> Optional[CustomMutator] # weighted random choice
      record_success(self, name: str) -> float         # weight *= SUCCESS_FACTOR (1.1)
      record_failure(self, name: str) -> float         # weight *= FAILURE_FACTOR (0.99), floor MIN_WEIGHT (0.1)
      stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]
      __len__ / __contains__
      module constants: SUCCESS_FACTOR = 1.1, FAILURE_FACTOR = 0.99, MIN_WEIGHT = 0.1
  class GrammarMutator(CustomMutator)      # token templates, structured input generation,
                                           # grammar-aware trim (drop whole tokens, not bytes)
  class CmpLogMutator(CustomMutator)       # CmpLog/RedQueen: record comparison operands seen at
                                           # runtime and substitute them into the buffer to get past
                                           # magic-byte checks. Needs: record_cmp(operand_a, operand_b),
                                           # observe(buf) / colorization, and an operand table.
  class HavocMutator(CustomMutator)        # thin wrapper over AFL's own havoc (a sensible default entry
                                           # in the registry)
  class CustomMutatorFuzzer(AFLFuzzer)     # AFL++ with the custom-mutator stage: overrides havoc_stage
                                           # (or adds a custom stage) to draw a mutator from the registry,
                                           # call fuzz()/havoc_mutation()/post_process(), feed results back
                                           # via record_success/record_failure and queue_new_entry().
                                           # ctor kwarg: registry: Optional[MutatorRegistry] = None
                                           # exposes .registry and extends stats() with mutator info.

fuzzsim/aflpp_mopt.py
  MOPT_OPERATORS: List[str] = ["bit_flip", "byte_flip", "arith_add", "arith_sub",
                               "interesting", "random_byte", "havoc_1", "havoc_2"]
  constants: W_INIT = 0.9, W_END = 0.3, W_NOW/inertia handling, C1 = 1.3, C2 = 1.3,
             V_MIN = -0.3, V_MAX = 0.3, P_MIN = 0.02, P_MAX = 0.50,
             PILOT_PERIOD (L, execs per pilot iteration), SWARM_NUM (e.g. 5), PERIOD_CORE
  class Particle          # one swarm particle: position[], velocity[], pbest_position[], pbest_fitness,
                          # update_velocity(gbest, w, c1, c2, rng), update_position(), clamp helpers,
                          # normalise() so positions form a valid probability distribution in [P_MIN, P_MAX]
  class MOptScheduler     # PSO over the operator probability simplex
      __init__(self, operators=MOPT_OPERATORS, swarm_num=SWARM_NUM, seed=42, pilot_period=..., ...)
      phase: "pilot" | "core"
      select_operator(self, rng=None) -> str        # sample from the current distribution
      record_result(self, operator: str, found_new: bool) -> None
      step(self) -> None                            # advance the schedule; drives pilot->core transition
      pso_update(self) -> None                      # v = w*v + c1*r1*(pbest-x) + c2*r2*(gbest-x); x += v
      fitness(self, ...) -> float                   # new-paths-per-exec of an operator/particle
      gbest / gbest_fitness, personal bests, fitness_history: List[float]
      has_converged(self) -> bool
      probabilities(self) -> Dict[str, float]
      stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]
  class MOptMutator       # applies one named operator to a buffer (the 8 operators above)
  class MOptFuzzer(AFLFuzzer)   # havoc_stage driven by MOptScheduler.select_operator; feeds
                                # record_result back; ctor kwargs: swarm_num, pilot_period, mode
  class PowerScheduleEnsemble   # rotates through FAST/COE/EXPLORE/QUAD/LINEAR per queue cycle,
                                # using fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules.PowerSchedule + EnergyComputer.
                                # API: __init__(schedules=None, ...), current() -> PowerSchedule,
                                # advance(cycle: int) -> PowerSchedule, energy(alpha, freq, sel) -> float,
                                # history: List[PowerSchedule], stats()
  class AFLPlusPlusFuzzer(MOptFuzzer)  # optional: MOpt + custom mutators + ensemble schedule together


YOUR TASK: create ONLY the file /workspace/fuzzsim/aflpp_mopt.py.

Implement MOpt's PSO-based mutation scheduling exactly as listed in the contract, plus
PowerScheduleEnsemble.

Details that matter (from the MOpt paper, Lyu et al., USENIX Sec'19, and AFL++'s afl-fuzz-mopt.c):
- Pilot phase: each swarm tests the operators independently for L executions each, measuring
  fitness = (number of new paths/interesting inputs found) / (number of executions) per operator.
  After the pilot period the best swarm becomes the global best and the scheduler moves to the core phase.
- Core phase: continuous PSO. velocity update v = w*v + c1*r1*(pbest - x) + c2*r2*(gbest - x),
  position update x = x + v, velocity clamped to [V_MIN, V_MAX] = [-0.3, 0.3], probabilities clamped
  to [P_MIN, P_MAX] = [0.02, 0.50] and then normalised so they sum to 1 (renormalisation must respect
  the bounds -- document how you handle a distribution that cannot satisfy both).
- Inertia weight w decays linearly from W_INIT to W_END over the run.
- Track personal bests per particle, a global best, a fitness_history list and a has_converged()
  monitor (e.g. gbest fitness unchanged for N updates, or swarm spread below a threshold).
- MOptMutator applies exactly the 8 named operators to a bytes buffer using numpy RandomState.
- MOptFuzzer subclasses AFLFuzzer and replaces the havoc stage: for each iteration select an operator
  from the scheduler's current distribution, apply it (stacked 2..2^7 times like havoc), execute, and
  report whether it found something new.
- PowerScheduleEnsemble rotates FAST -> COE -> EXPLORE -> QUAD -> LINEAR per queue cycle and computes
  energy through fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules.EnergyComputer.

Verify your work by running, from /workspace:
  python3 -c "from fuzzsim.aflpp_mopt import *; print('ok')"
and a short smoke run of MOptFuzzer on CrashmeProgram with max_execs=3000, seed=42, printing stats
plus the operator probability distribution before/after. Iterate until clean. Report the final
public API you actually wrote.

1	"""AFLFast power schedules derived from the Markov-chain model of fuzzing.
2	
3	Bohme, Pham and Roychoudhury (CCS'16) model greybox fuzzing as a Markov
4	chain whose *states* are the execution paths a program can take and whose
5	*transitions* are "mutating an input exercising path ``i`` yields an input
6	exercising path ``j``".  Under that model AFL's constant energy is wasteful:
7	it keeps spending the same budget on seeds whose path is already exercised
8	by a huge fraction of all generated inputs.  AFLFast instead assigns energy
9	
10	* inversely proportional to the *path frequency* ``f(i)`` -- the number of
11	  generated inputs that exercised path ``i`` -- so high-density regions of
12	  the chain are abandoned quickly, and
13	* monotonically (exponentially, linearly or quadratically) in the
14	  *selection count* ``s(i)`` -- the number of times seed ``i`` has been
15	  chosen -- so a seed that keeps being picked without paying off is given
16	  the chance to escape its local basin before being dropped.
17	
18	The six schedules of the paper, with ``alpha(i)`` = AFL's own performance
19	score, ``beta`` a normalising constant and ``M`` an upper bound on energy:
20	
21	======== =====================================================
22	EXPLOIT  ``p(i) = alpha(i)``                    (plain AFL)
23	EXPLORE  ``p(i) = alpha(i) / beta``             (constant, low)
24	COE      ``p(i) = 0`` if ``f(i) > mu`` else ``min(alpha/beta * 2^s, M)``
25	FAST     ``p(i) = min(alpha/beta * 2^s(i) / f(i), M)``   (recommended)
26	LINEAR   ``p(i) = min(alpha/beta * s(i) / f(i), M)``
27	QUAD     ``p(i) = min(alpha/beta * s(i)^2 / f(i), M)``
28	======== =====================================================
29	
30	``mu`` is the mean path frequency over the queue; COE's cut-off simply
31	refuses to spend anything on a seed whose path is exercised more often
32	than average.  ``M`` exists because ``2^s`` explodes: without it a seed
33	picked twenty times would monopolise the whole campaign.
34	
35	Frequency units
36	---------------
37	``f(i)`` is expressed in units of ``mu`` (i.e. the *relative* frequency
38	``f(i)/mu``) rather than as a raw execution count.  The two differ only by
39	a global constant, but the normalised form makes the energies independent
40	of how long the campaign has been running and of how many states the
41	target has -- essential for the tiny simulated targets used here, where a
42	raw count reaches the thousands within seconds.  ``f(i)/mu == 1`` is
43	exactly the COE cut-off, so all six schedules share one scale.
44	
45	Determinism: this module is pure arithmetic; no randomness is involved.
46	"""
47	
48	from __future__ import annotations
49	
50	import math
51	from dataclasses import dataclass
52	from enum import Enum
53	from typing import Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence
54	
55	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	# Documented constants
57	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	
59	#: Normalising constant ``beta`` of the paper.  AFLFast's reference
60	#: implementation exposes it as ``POWER_BETA`` and ships ``1`` as the
61	#: default: energy is measured directly in AFL "performance score" units
62	#: where 100 == one baseline havoc round.
63	POWER_BETA = 1.0
64	
65	#: Upper bound ``M`` on the energy of a single seed.  The paper leaves ``M``
66	#: free; it only has to stop ``2^s`` from letting one seed monopolise the
67	#: campaign.  AFL's havoc stage runs ``HAVOC_CYCLES * p / 100`` mutations, so
68	#: energy is naturally read in "baseline havoc rounds": ``M = 225`` allows a
69	#: seed at most 2.25 rounds (576 stacked mutations) per selection.  A value
70	#: in the 2-3x band keeps the exponential schedule a *re-weighting* of AFL's
71	#: budget rather than a replacement for it; 225 is the point in that band
72	#: calibrated on the reference ``crashme`` target, where it leaves roughly a
73	#: third of the corpus below the cap (an all-capped queue would make FAST
74	#: degenerate into a constant schedule again).
75	ENERGY_CAP_M = 225.0
76	
77	#: ``2^s`` is only allowed to grow while ``s < FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP``; beyond that
78	#: the factor is frozen.  Mirrors AFL++'s ``q->fuzz_level < 16`` guard and
79	#: keeps the arithmetic in float range.
80	FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP = 16
81	
82	#: Seeds whose relative frequency is below this fraction of ``mu`` count as
83	#: *rare* paths and receive :data:`RARE_PATH_BONUS` extra energy.
84	RARE_PATH_RATIO = 0.25
85	
86	#: Multiplicative bonus handed to a rare path (applied to ``alpha``).
87	RARE_PATH_BONUS = 2.0
88	
89	#: Smallest relative frequency we will divide by (a path observed once,
90	#: while ``mu`` is huge, must not produce an infinite energy).
91	MIN_RELATIVE_FREQ = 1e-6
92	
93	
94	class PowerSchedule(str, Enum):
95	    """The six AFLFast power schedules (``-p`` in afl-fuzz)."""
96	
97	    EXPLOIT = "exploit"
98	    EXPLORE = "explore"
99	    COE = "coe"
100	    FAST = "fast"
101	    LINEAR = "linear"
102	    QUAD = "quad"
103	
104	
105	#: Canonical ordering used by the comparison utilities / reports.
106	SCHEDULE_ORDER: List[PowerSchedule] = [
107	    PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT,
108	    PowerSchedule.EXPLORE,
109	    PowerSchedule.COE,
110	    PowerSchedule.FAST,
111	    PowerSchedule.LINEAR,
112	    PowerSchedule.QUAD,
113	]
114	
115	#: One-line description of what each schedule does, for reports.
116	SCHEDULE_DOC: Dict[PowerSchedule, str] = {
117	    PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT: "p = alpha (AFL's constant schedule)",
118	    PowerSchedule.EXPLORE: "p = alpha / beta (constant, deliberately low)",
119	    PowerSchedule.COE: "p = 0 if f > mu else min(alpha/beta * 2^s, M)",
120	    PowerSchedule.FAST: "p = min(alpha/beta * 2^s / f, M)",
121	    PowerSchedule.LINEAR: "p = min(alpha/beta * s / f, M)",
122	    PowerSchedule.QUAD: "p = min(alpha/beta * s^2 / f, M)",
123	}
124	
125	#: Schedules that order the queue by ``s(i)`` (see
126	#: :func:`fuzzsim.aflfast_search.prioritize_small_s`); the remaining ones
127	#: order by ``f(i)``.
128	S_PRIORITIZED_SCHEDULES = frozenset({PowerSchedule.FAST, PowerSchedule.COE})
129	
130	
131	def schedule_from_name(name: str) -> PowerSchedule:
132	    """Parse a schedule name (case-insensitive), raising on unknown ones."""
133	    try:
134	        return PowerSchedule(str(name).strip().lower())
135	    except ValueError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
136	        raise ValueError(f"unknown power schedule {name!r}") from exc
137	
138	
139	def describe_schedule(schedule: PowerSchedule) -> str:
140	    """Return the formula of ``schedule`` as a human-readable string."""
141	    return SCHEDULE_DOC[PowerSchedule(schedule)]
142	
143	
144	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
145	# Energy assignment
146	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
147	
148	@dataclass
149	class ScheduleInputs:
150	    """The four quantities every AFLFast schedule is a function of.
151	
152	    ``alpha`` is AFL's performance score for the seed, ``freq`` is ``f(i)``
153	    expressed relative to ``mu`` (see the module docstring), ``sel`` is
154	    ``s(i)`` and ``mu_ratio`` is the cut-off reference: COE skips a seed
155	    when ``freq > mu_ratio``.  Keeping ``mu_ratio`` explicit (rather than
156	    hard-coding ``1.0``) lets callers experiment with a laxer cut-off.
157	    """
158	
159	    alpha: float
160	    freq: float
161	    sel: int
162	    mu_ratio: float = 1.0
163	
164	
165	def _exp_factor(sel: int) -> float:
166	    """``2^s`` with AFL++'s ``fuzz_level`` freeze at :data:`FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP`."""
167	    return float(1 << min(max(int(sel), 0), FUZZ_LEVEL_CAP))
168	
169	
170	def _safe_freq(freq: float) -> float:
171	    """Clamp a relative frequency away from zero before dividing by it."""
172	    return max(float(freq), MIN_RELATIVE_FREQ)
173	
174	
175	def schedule_energy(schedule: PowerSchedule,
176	                    alpha: float,
177	                    freq: float,
178	                    sel: int,
179	                    mu_ratio: float = 1.0,
180	                    beta: float = POWER_BETA,
181	                    energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M) -> float:
182	    """Energy ``p(i)`` assigned to a seed by ``schedule``.
183	
184	    ``alpha`` is AFL's perf score, ``freq`` is ``f(i)/mu``, ``sel`` is
185	    ``s(i)``, ``beta`` the normalising constant and ``energy_cap`` the
186	    upper bound ``M``.  Every schedule other than EXPLOIT/EXPLORE is
187	    clamped to ``[0, M]``.
188	    """
189	    schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
190	    alpha = max(0.0, float(alpha))
191	    beta = max(beta, 1e-9)
192	    base = alpha / beta
193	    f = _safe_freq(freq)
194	    s = max(int(sel), 0)
195	
196	    if schedule is PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT:
197	        # AFL's own constant schedule: the perf score, unchanged.
198	        return alpha
199	    if schedule is PowerSchedule.EXPLORE:
200	        # Constant but scaled down: spend little everywhere, cover a lot.
201	        return base
202	    if schedule is PowerSchedule.COE:
203	        # Cut-off exponential: nothing at all for above-average paths.
204	        if f > mu_ratio:
205	            return 0.0
206	        return min(base * _exp_factor(s), energy_cap)
207	    if schedule is PowerSchedule.FAST:
208	        return min(base * _exp_factor(s) / f, energy_cap)
209	    if schedule is PowerSchedule.LINEAR:
210	        return min(base * s / f, energy_cap)
211	    # QUAD
212	    return min(base * (s * s) / f, energy_cap)

219	def gini_coefficient(values: Sequence[float]) -> float:
220	    """Gini coefficient of ``values`` (0 = perfectly even, 1 = winner-takes-all).
221	
222	    Computed with the sorted "relative mean absolute difference" form
223	    ``G = (2 * sum(i * x_i) / (n * sum(x))) - (n + 1) / n`` for ``x``
224	    sorted ascending and ``i`` one-based.  Negative values are not
225	    meaningful for energies, so the input is clamped at 0.
226	    """
227	    xs = sorted(max(0.0, float(v)) for v in values)
228	    n = len(xs)
229	    if n == 0:
230	        return 0.0
231	    total = sum(xs)
232	    if total <= 0.0:
233	        return 0.0
234	    weighted = sum((i + 1) * x for i, x in enumerate(xs))
235	    return (2.0 * weighted) / (n * total) - (n + 1) / n
236	
237	
238	def energy_summary(values: Sequence[float],
239	                   energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M) -> Dict[str, float]:
240	    """Descriptive statistics of an energy distribution."""
241	    vals = [float(v) for v in values]
242	    n = len(vals)
243	    if n == 0:
244	        return {"count": 0, "total": 0.0, "mean": 0.0, "min": 0.0, "max": 0.0,
245	                "stdev": 0.0, "gini": 0.0, "capped_fraction": 0.0,
246	                "zero_fraction": 0.0}
247	    mean = sum(vals) / n
248	    var = sum((v - mean) ** 2 for v in vals) / n
249	    return {
250	        "count": n,
251	        "total": sum(vals),
252	        "mean": mean,
253	        "min": min(vals),
254	        "max": max(vals),
255	        "stdev": math.sqrt(var),
256	        "gini": gini_coefficient(vals),
257	        "capped_fraction": sum(1 for v in vals if v >= energy_cap - 1e-9) / n,
258	        "zero_fraction": sum(1 for v in vals if v <= 0.0) / n,
259	    }

262	class EnergyComputer:
263	    """Applies one power schedule to a whole queue and analyses the result.
264	
265	    The computer owns the schedule and its two constants (``beta``, ``M``)
266	    so that the fuzzer, the experiment and the tests all agree on them.
267	    """
268	
269	    def __init__(self,
270	                 schedule: PowerSchedule = PowerSchedule.FAST,
271	                 beta: float = POWER_BETA,
272	                 energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
273	                 mu_ratio: float = 1.0,
274	                 rare_ratio: float = RARE_PATH_RATIO,
275	                 rare_bonus: float = RARE_PATH_BONUS):
276	        self.schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
277	        self.beta = float(beta)
278	        self.energy_cap = float(energy_cap)
279	        self.mu_ratio = float(mu_ratio)
280	        self.rare_ratio = float(rare_ratio)
281	        self.rare_bonus = float(rare_bonus)
282	
283	    # -- single seed ------------------------------------------------------
284	    def is_rare(self, freq: float) -> bool:
285	        """A path is rare when it is exercised far less often than average."""
286	        return float(freq) < self.rare_ratio * self.mu_ratio
287	
288	    def energy(self, alpha: float, freq: float, sel: int,
289	               apply_rare_bonus: bool = True) -> float:
290	        """Energy for one seed, including the rare-path bonus on ``alpha``."""
291	        if apply_rare_bonus and self.is_rare(freq):
292	            alpha = alpha * self.rare_bonus
293	        return schedule_energy(self.schedule, alpha, freq, sel,
294	                               mu_ratio=self.mu_ratio, beta=self.beta,
295	                               energy_cap=self.energy_cap)
296	
297	    def energy_of(self, spec: ScheduleInputs,
298	                  apply_rare_bonus: bool = True) -> float:
299	        """Energy for a :class:`ScheduleInputs` record."""
300	        return self.energy(spec.alpha, spec.freq, spec.sel,
301	                           apply_rare_bonus=apply_rare_bonus)
302	
303	    # -- whole queue ------------------------------------------------------
304	    def compute_all(self, specs: Iterable[ScheduleInputs],
305	                    apply_rare_bonus: bool = True) -> List[float]:
306	        """Energies for a whole queue, in queue order."""
307	        return [self.energy_of(spec, apply_rare_bonus) for spec in specs]
308	
309	    def gini(self, specs: Iterable[ScheduleInputs]) -> float:
310	        """Gini coefficient of the energy distribution over ``specs``."""
311	        return gini_coefficient(self.compute_all(specs))
312	
313	    def summary(self, specs: Iterable[ScheduleInputs]) -> Dict[str, float]:
314	        """Descriptive statistics of the energy distribution over ``specs``."""
315	        return energy_summary(self.compute_all(specs), self.energy_cap)
316

322	def compare_schedules(specs: Sequence[ScheduleInputs],
323	                      schedules: Optional[Sequence[PowerSchedule]] = None,
324	                      beta: float = POWER_BETA,
325	                      energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
326	                      mu_ratio: float = 1.0) -> Dict[PowerSchedule, Dict[str, float]]:
327	    """Summarise the energy distribution each schedule would produce.
328	
329	    Handy for showing *why* FAST behaves differently from EXPLOIT on the
330	    same queue: identical inputs, six different distributions.
331	    """
332	    chosen = list(schedules) if schedules is not None else list(SCHEDULE_ORDER)
333	    out: Dict[PowerSchedule, Dict[str, float]] = {}
334	    for sched in chosen:
335	        computer = EnergyComputer(sched, beta=beta, energy_cap=energy_cap,
336	                                  mu_ratio=mu_ratio)
337	        out[PowerSchedule(sched)] = computer.summary(specs)
338	    return out

342	                          beta: float = POWER_BETA,
343	                          energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
344	                          mu_ratio: float = 1.0) -> Dict[PowerSchedule, List[float]]:

2	
3	A faithful, deterministic simulation of AFL's algorithm on top of the
4	simulated targets in :mod:`fuzzsim.targets`.  The implementation follows
5	``afl-fuzz.c`` closely:
6	
7	* 64KB shared-memory coverage bitmap with hit-count bucketing
8	* edge identification via ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)``
9	* fork server model (one-time handshake, snapshot re-use per exec)
10	* test case calibration with variable-behaviour (stability) detection
11	* input trimming with powers-of-two block removal
12	* corpus culling via greedy set cover over ``top_rated`` entries
13	* deterministic stages: bitflip 1/2/4, byte flip 8/16/32, arithmetic
14	  add/sub for 8/16/32 bit widths in both endiannesses, interesting
15	  values 8/16/32, user dictionary overwrite/insert, auto dictionary
16	* auto-dictionary (token) extraction during the walking bit flip stage
17	* havoc stage with stacked random mutations (2^1 .. 2^7 per round)
18	* splice stage (two seeds combined at a midpoint, followed by havoc)
19	* performance scoring from exec speed / bitmap size / depth / handicap
20	* crash de-duplication via the crash coverage hash
21	
22	Determinism: every random decision is drawn from a ``numpy.random.RandomState``
23	seeded by the caller (the experiments use seed 42).
24	"""

81	def classify_count(count: int) -> int:
82	    """Bucket a raw hit count into AFL's power-of-two-ish classes.
83	
84	    Buckets: 1, 2, 3, 4-7, 8-15, 16-31, 32-127, 128+.
85	    """
86	    if count <= 0:
87	        return 0
88	    if count == 1:
89	        return 1
90	    if count == 2:
91	        return 2
92	    if count == 3:
93	        return 4
94	    if count <= 7:
95	        return 8
96	    if count <= 15:
97	        return 16
98	    if count <= 31:
99	        return 32
100	    if count <= 127:
101	        return 64
102	    return 128

114	def afl_edge_index(prev_loc: int, cur_loc: int, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE) -> int:
115	    """AFL's edge hash: ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)`` modulo the map size.
116	
117	    The right shift keeps ``A->B`` and ``B->A`` distinguishable and stops
118	    self-loops from folding onto index 0.
119	    """
120	    return (cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)) & (map_size - 1)

125	    items = sorted(trace.items())
126	    payload = ",".join(f"{idx}:{cnt}" for idx, cnt in items).encode()
127	    return hashlib.sha1(payload).hexdigest()[:16]

130	class AFLBitmap:
131	    """Sparse view of AFL's 64KB shared-memory bitmap.
132	
133	    ``virgin_bits`` starts as all ``0xff`` (nothing seen yet); observing a
134	    bucket clears the corresponding bit.  Only touched indices are stored so
135	    the 64KB map costs nothing for the tiny simulated targets.
136	    """
137	
138	    def __init__(self, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
139	        self.map_size = map_size
140	        self.virgin: Dict[int, int] = {}
141	        self.covered: Set[int] = set()
142	
143	    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
144	    def has_new_bits(self, trace: Dict[int, int]) -> int:
145	        """Return 2 for a brand new edge, 1 for a new hit-count bucket, else 0."""
146	        ret = 0
147	        for idx, cnt in classify_counts(trace).items():
148	            virgin = self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
149	            if virgin & cnt:
150	                if virgin == 0xFF:
151	                    ret = 2
152	                elif ret < 1:
153	                    ret = 1
154	        return ret
155	
156	    def update(self, trace: Dict[int, int]) -> Set[int]:
157	        """Fold a trace into the bitmap, returning the newly covered indices."""
158	        new_edges: Set[int] = set()
159	        for idx, cnt in classify_counts(trace).items():
160	            virgin = self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
161	            if virgin == 0xFF:
162	                new_edges.add(idx)
163	            self.virgin[idx] = virgin & ~cnt
164	            self.covered.add(idx)
165	        return new_edges
166	
167	    def count_bytes(self) -> int:
168	        """Number of bitmap bytes that have been touched (edges covered)."""
169	        return len(self.covered)
170	
171	    def coverage_percentage(self, total_edges: int) -> float:
172	        if total_edges <= 0:
173	            return 0.0
174	        return len(self.covered) / total_edges * 100.0
175	
176	    def to_bytes(self) -> bytearray:
177	        """Materialise the full 64KB map (used by tests / debugging)."""
178	        buf = bytearray(self.map_size)
179	        for idx in self.covered:
180	            buf[idx] = 0xFF & ~self.virgin.get(idx, 0xFF)
181	        return buf
182	
183	    def reset(self) -> None:
184	        self.virgin.clear()
185	        self.covered.clear()

203	class ForkServer:
204	    """Simulated AFL fork server.
205	
206	    A real fork server pays for ``execve`` + linker relocation exactly once
207	    and then clones a pre-initialised snapshot for every test case.  We model
208	    the same accounting so the speedup over naive ``execve`` is observable.
209	    """
210	
211	    EXECVE_COST_US = 2500.0  # cost of a full process spawn
212	    FORK_COST_US = 120.0  # cost of cloning the snapshot
213	
214	    def __init__(self, target: Any, map_size: int = MAP_SIZE):
215	        self.target = target
216	        self.map_size = map_size
217	        self.started = False
218	        self.handshake_cost_us = 0.0
219	        self.total_execs = 0
220	        self.total_forks = 0
221	        self.total_crashes = 0
222	        self.total_hangs = 0
223	        self.child_timeout = EXEC_TIMEOUT
224	        self.edge_index: Dict[int, int] = {}
225	        self.index_edge: Dict[int, int] = {}
226	        self._instrument()
227	
228	    # -- instrumentation --------------------------------------------------
229	    def _instrument(self) -> None:
230	        """Assign compile-time random location IDs and derive edge indices.
231	
232	        Mirrors afl-as.h: each basic block gets ``R(MAP_SIZE)`` and every edge
233	        lands at ``cur_loc ^ (prev_loc >> 1)``.  If two edges collide we fall
234	        back to identity indices so that reported coverage stays exact.
235	        """
236	        program = getattr(self.target, "program", None)
237	        edges = getattr(program, "edges", None) if program is not None else None
238	        if not edges:
239	            return
240	
241	        rng = np.random.RandomState(0xA51)
242	        block_ids = sorted({e.src for e in edges} | {e.dst for e in edges})
243	        locs = {bid: int(rng.randint(0, self.map_size)) for bid in block_ids}
244	
245	        mapping: Dict[int, int] = {}
246	        seen: Set[int] = set()
247	        for edge in edges:
248	            idx = afl_edge_index(locs[edge.src], locs[edge.dst], self.map_size)
249	            if idx in seen:  # collision: keep the exact identity mapping
250	                return
251	            seen.add(idx)
252	            mapping[edge.edge_id] = idx
253	
254	        self.edge_index = mapping
255	        self.index_edge = {idx: eid for eid, idx in mapping.items()}
256	
257	    def index_of(self, edge_id: int) -> int:
258	        return self.edge_index.get(edge_id, edge_id)
259	
260	    def edge_of(self, index: int) -> int:
261	        return self.index_edge.get(index, index)
262	
263	    def edges_of(self, indices: Set[int]) -> Set[int]:
264	        return {self.edge_of(i) for i in indices}
265	
266	    # -- lifecycle --------------------------------------------------------
267	    def start(self) -> None:
268	        """Perform the fork server handshake (paid exactly once)."""
269	        if not self.started:
270	            self.started = True
271	            self.handshake_cost_us = self.EXECVE_COST_US
272	
273	    def run(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
274	        """Run the target once, returning the classified execution result."""
275	        if not self.started:
276	            self.start()
277	
278	        edges, is_crash, exec_time = self.target.execute(bytes(data))
279	        self.total_execs += 1
280	        self.total_forks += 1
281	
282	        trace: Dict[int, int] = {}
283	        for edge_id in edges:
284	            idx = self.index_of(edge_id)
285	            trace[idx] = trace.get(idx, 0) + 1
286	
287	        exec_us = exec_time * 1e6 + self.FORK_COST_US
288	        is_hang = exec_time > self.child_timeout
289	        if is_crash:
290	            self.total_crashes += 1
291	        if is_hang:
292	            self.total_hangs += 1
293	
294	        return ExecResult(trace=trace, edges=set(edges), is_crash=is_crash,
295	                          is_hang=is_hang, exec_us=exec_us)
296	
297	    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
298	    def time_without_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
299	        return self.total_execs * self.EXECVE_COST_US
300	
301	    def time_with_forkserver_us(self) -> float:
302	        return self.EXECVE_COST_US + self.total_execs * self.FORK_COST_US
303	
304	    def speedup(self) -> float:
305	        with_fs = self.time_with_forkserver_us()
306	        if with_fs <= 0:
307	            return 1.0
308	        return self.time_without_forkserver_us() / with_fs

404	def _could_be_bitflip(xor_val: int) -> bool:
405	    """AFL's ``could_be_bitflip``: is the delta reachable by the bitflip stage?"""
406	    sh = 0
407	    if not xor_val:
408	        return True
409	    while (xor_val & 1) == 0:
410	        sh += 1
411	        xor_val >>= 1
412	    if xor_val in (1, 3, 15):
413	        return True
414	    if sh & 7:
415	        return False
416	    return xor_val in (0xFF, 0xFFFF, 0xFFFFFFFF)
417

419	def _could_be_arith(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int) -> bool:
420	    """AFL's ``could_be_arith``: is the delta reachable by the arith stage?"""
421	    if old_val == new_val:
422	        return True
423	    diffs = 0
424	    ov = nv = 0
425	    for i in range(blen):
426	        a = (old_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
427	        b = (new_val >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF
428	        if a != b:
429	            diffs += 1
430	            ov, nv = a, b
431	    if diffs == 1:
432	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
433	            return True
434	    if blen == 1:
435	        return False
436	
437	    diffs = 0
438	    for i in range(blen // 2):
439	        a = (old_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
440	        b = (new_val >> (16 * i)) & 0xFFFF
441	        if a != b:
442	            diffs += 1
443	            ov, nv = a, b
444	    if diffs == 1:
445	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
446	            return True
447	        ov = ((ov >> 8) | (ov << 8)) & 0xFFFF
448	        nv = ((nv >> 8) | (nv << 8)) & 0xFFFF
449	        if ((ov - nv) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX or ((nv - ov) & 0xFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
450	            return True
451	    if blen == 2:
452	        return False
453	
454	    if ((old_val - new_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
455	        return True
456	    if ((new_val - old_val) & 0xFFFFFFFF) <= ARITH_MAX:
457	        return True
458	    return False

461	def _could_be_interest(old_val: int, new_val: int, blen: int, check_le: bool) -> bool:
462	    """AFL's ``could_be_interest``: is the delta reachable by the interest stage?"""
463	    if old_val == new_val:
464	        return True
465	    for i in range(blen):
466	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_8:
467	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFF) << (8 * i))
468	            if new_val == tval:
469	                return True
470	    if blen == 2 and not check_le:
471	        return False
472	    for i in range(blen - 1):
473	        for j in mutation_ops.INTERESTING_16:
474	            tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | ((j & 0xFFFF) << (8 * i))
475	            if new_val == tval:
476	                return True
477	            if blen > 2:
478	                swapped = ((j & 0xFF) << 8) | ((j >> 8) & 0xFF)
479	                tval = (old_val & ~(0xFFFF << (8 * i))) | (swapped << (8 * i))
480	                if new_val == tval:
481	                    return True
482	    return False

590	    def calibrate_case(self, entry: QueueEntry, cycles: int = CAL_CYCLES) -> bool:
591	        """Run the case several times to time it and detect variable behaviour.
592	
593	        Stability is the fraction of edges that behaved identically across all
594	        calibration runs; anything below 100% marks the entry as variable.
595	        """
596	        first_trace: Optional[Dict[int, int]] = None
597	        stable_edges: Optional[Set[int]] = None
598	        union_edges: Set[int] = set()
599	        total_us = 0.0
600	        runs = 0
601	        var_detected = False
602	
603	        for _ in range(max(1, cycles)):
604	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
605	            runs += 1
606	            total_us += res.exec_us
607	            classified = classify_counts(res.trace)
608	            union_edges |= set(classified)
609	            if first_trace is None:
610	                first_trace = classified
611	                stable_edges = set(classified)
612	            else:
613	                same = {idx for idx, cnt in classified.items()
614	                        if first_trace.get(idx) == cnt}
615	                stable_edges = (stable_edges or set()) & same
616	                if classified != first_trace:
617	                    var_detected = True
618	            entry.is_crash = entry.is_crash or res.is_crash
619	
620	        assert first_trace is not None
621	        entry.trace = dict(first_trace)
622	        entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(first_trace))
623	        entry.exec_us = total_us / max(1, runs)
624	        entry.exec_time = entry.exec_us / 1e6
625	        entry.bitmap_size = len(first_trace)
626	        entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(first_trace)
627	        entry.var_behavior = var_detected
628	        entry.stability = (100.0 if not union_edges
629	                           else len(stable_edges or set()) / len(union_edges) * 100.0)
630	        if var_detected and entry.cal_failed == 0:
631	            entry.cal_failed = 1
632	
633	        if not entry.is_crash:
634	            new_edges = self.bitmap.update(entry.trace)
635	            entry.unique_edges = self.fork_server.edges_of(new_edges)
636	            self.coverage_history.append((self.total_execs,
637	                                          self.bitmap.count_bytes()))
638	        self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
639	        return not var_detected

641	    def trim_case(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> int:
642	        """Powers-of-two block removal that preserves the execution checksum.
643	
644	        Returns the number of bytes removed.
645	        """
646	        if entry.trim_done or len(entry.data) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
647	            entry.trim_done = True
648	            return 0
649	
650	        self.current_stage = "trim"
651	        data = bytearray(entry.data)
652	        orig_len = len(data)
653	        ref_cksum = entry.exec_cksum
654	
655	        len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
656	        remove_len = max(len_p2 // TRIM_START_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES)
657	
658	        while remove_len >= max(len_p2 // TRIM_END_STEPS, TRIM_MIN_BYTES):
659	            pos = remove_len
660	            while pos < len(data):
661	                trim_avail = min(remove_len, len(data) - pos)
662	                candidate = bytes(data[:pos]) + bytes(data[pos + trim_avail:])
663	                if len(candidate) < TRIM_MIN_BYTES:
664	                    pos += remove_len
665	                    continue
666	                res = self.run_target(candidate)
667	                if hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace)) == ref_cksum:
668	                    data = bytearray(candidate)
669	                    len_p2 = 1 << max(0, int(len(data) - 1).bit_length())
670	                else:
671	                    pos += remove_len
672	            remove_len //= 2
673	            if remove_len == 0:
674	                break
675	
676	        removed = orig_len - len(data)
677	        if removed:
678	            entry.data = bytes(data)
679	            res = self.run_target(entry.data)
680	            entry.trace = classify_counts(res.trace)
681	            entry.coverage = self.fork_server.edges_of(set(entry.trace))
682	            entry.bitmap_size = len(entry.trace)
683	            entry.exec_cksum = hash_trace(entry.trace)
684	            self.update_bitmap_score(entry)
685	        entry.trim_done = True
686	        return removed

688	    def update_bitmap_score(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> None:
689	        """Track the smallest+fastest entry covering each edge (``top_rated``)."""
690	        fav_factor = entry.exec_us * max(1, entry.size)
691	        for idx in entry.trace:
692	            current = self.top_rated.get(idx)
693	            if current is not None:
694	                if fav_factor > current.exec_us * max(1, current.size):
695	                    continue
696	                if (fav_factor == current.exec_us * max(1, current.size)
697	                        and current.index <= entry.index):
698	                    continue
699	            self.top_rated[idx] = entry
700	            self.score_changed = True
701	
702	    def cull_queue(self) -> List[QueueEntry]:
703	        """Greedy set cover: pick a minimal favored subset covering every edge."""
704	        if not self.score_changed:
705	            return [q for q in self.queue if q.favored]
706	
707	        self.score_changed = False
708	        for entry in self.queue:
709	            entry.favored = False
710	            entry.is_favored = False
711	
712	        temp_v: Set[int] = set(self.bitmap.covered)
713	        favored: List[QueueEntry] = []
714	        for idx in sorted(self.bitmap.covered):
715	            if idx not in temp_v:
716	                continue
717	            best = self.top_rated.get(idx)
718	            if best is None:
719	                temp_v.discard(idx)
720	                continue
721	            if not best.favored:
722	                best.favored = True
723	                best.is_favored = True
724	                favored.append(best)
725	            temp_v -= set(best.trace)
726	
727	        self.queued_favored = len(favored)
728	        self.pending_favored = sum(1 for q in favored if not q.was_fuzzed)
729	        return favored

731	    # -- scoring ----------------------------------------------------------
732	    def calculate_score(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> float:
733	        """AFL's ``calculate_score``: perf score from speed, size, depth, age."""
734	        if not self.queue:
735	            return 100.0
736	        avg_exec_us = sum(q.exec_us for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
737	        avg_bitmap_size = sum(q.bitmap_size for q in self.queue) / len(self.queue)
738	        avg_bitmap_size = max(avg_bitmap_size, 1e-9)
739	
740	        perf_score = 100.0
741	        if entry.exec_us * 0.1 > avg_exec_us:
742	            perf_score = 10.0
743	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.25 > avg_exec_us:
744	            perf_score = 25.0
745	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.5 > avg_exec_us:
746	            perf_score = 50.0
747	        elif entry.exec_us * 0.75 > avg_exec_us:
748	            perf_score = 75.0
749	        elif entry.exec_us * 4 < avg_exec_us:
750	            perf_score = 300.0
751	        elif entry.exec_us * 3 < avg_exec_us:
752	            perf_score = 200.0
753	        elif entry.exec_us * 2 < avg_exec_us:
754	            perf_score = 150.0
755	
756	        if entry.bitmap_size * 0.3 > avg_bitmap_size:
757	            perf_score *= 3.0
758	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.5 > avg_bitmap_size:
759	            perf_score *= 2.0
760	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 0.75 > avg_bitmap_size:
761	            perf_score *= 1.5
762	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 3 < avg_bitmap_size:
763	            perf_score *= 0.25
764	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 2 < avg_bitmap_size:
765	            perf_score *= 0.5
766	        elif entry.bitmap_size * 1.5 < avg_bitmap_size:
767	            perf_score *= 0.75
768	
769	        if entry.handicap >= 4:
770	            perf_score *= 4.0
771	            entry.handicap -= 4
772	        elif entry.handicap:
773	            perf_score *= 2.0
774	            entry.handicap -= 1
775	
776	        if entry.depth <= 3:
777	            pass
778	        elif entry.depth <= 7:
779	            perf_score *= 2.0
780	        elif entry.depth <= 13:
781	            perf_score *= 3.0
782	        elif entry.depth <= 25:
783	            perf_score *= 4.0
784	        else:
785	            perf_score *= 5.0
786	
787	        if entry.stability < 100.0:
788	            perf_score *= max(0.25, entry.stability / 100.0)
789	
790	        return min(perf_score, HAVOC_MAX_MULT * 100.0)

841	    def deterministic_stages(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> int:
842	        """Run every deterministic stage over the entry, in AFL's order."""
843	        found = 0
844	        data = bytearray(entry.data)
845	        found += self._stage_bitflip1(entry, data)
846	        found += self._stage_bitflip_n(entry, data, 2)
847	        found += self._stage_bitflip_n(entry, data, 4)
848	        eff_map = self._stage_byteflip(entry, data)
849	        found += self._stage_byteflip_wide(entry, data, 2)
850	        found += self._stage_byteflip_wide(entry, data, 4)
851	        found += self._stage_arith(entry, data, 1, eff_map)
852	        found += self._stage_arith(entry, data, 2, eff_map)
853	        found += self._stage_arith(entry, data, 4, eff_map)
854	        found += self._stage_interest(entry, data, 1, eff_map)
855	        found += self._stage_interest(entry, data, 2, eff_map)
856	        found += self._stage_interest(entry, data, 4, eff_map)
857	        found += self._stage_extras(entry, data, eff_map)
858	        found += self._stage_auto_extras(entry, data)
859	        entry.passed_det = True
860	        return found

862	    def _stage_bitflip1(self, entry: QueueEntry, data: bytearray) -> int:
863	        """Walking single-bit flip; also collects auto-dictionary tokens."""
864	        self._stage("bitflip 1/1")
865	        found = 0
866	        nbits = len(data) * 8
867	        a_collect = bytearray()
868	        a_len = 0
869	        prev_cksum = entry.exec_cksum
870	
871	        for bit in range(nbits):
872	            buf = bytearray(data)
873	            byte_idx, bit_idx = bit >> 3, bit & 7
874	            buf[byte_idx] ^= 1 << bit_idx
875	            res = self.run_target(bytes(buf))
876	            found += self.save_if_interesting(bytes(buf), res, entry)
877	
878	            # Auto-dictionary extraction (AFL's token detection).
879	            if (bit & 7) == 7:
880	                cksum = hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace))
881	                if bit == nbits - 1 and cksum == prev_cksum:
882	                    if a_len < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
883	                        a_collect.append(data[bit >> 3])
884	                    a_len += 1
885	                    if MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= a_len <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
886	                        self.dictionary.maybe_add_auto(bytes(a_collect))
887	                elif cksum != prev_cksum:
888	                    if MIN_AUTO_EXTRA <= a_len <= MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
889	                        self.dictionary.maybe_add_auto(bytes(a_collect))
890	                    a_collect = bytearray()
891	                    a_len = 0
892	                    prev_cksum = cksum
893	                if cksum != entry.exec_cksum:
894	                    if a_len < MAX_AUTO_EXTRA:
895	                        a_collect.append(data[bit >> 3])
896	                    a_len += 1
897	        return found

899	    def _stage_bitflip_n(self, entry: QueueEntry, data: bytearray,
900	                         width: int) -> int:
901	        self._stage(f"bitflip {width}/1")
902	        found = 0
903	        nbits = len(data) * 8
904	        for bit in range(nbits - width + 1):
905	            buf = bytearray(data)
906	            for k in range(width):
907	                b = bit + k
908	                buf[b >> 3] ^= 1 << (b & 7)
909	            found += self.common_fuzz_stuff(bytes(buf), entry)
910	        return found

912	    def _stage_byteflip(self, entry: QueueEntry,
913	                        data: bytearray) -> List[bool]:
914	        """Byte flip 8/8, building the effector map as a side effect."""
915	        self._stage("bitflip 8/8")
916	        eff_map = [False] * len(data)
917	        for i in range(len(data)):
918	            buf = bytearray(data)
919	            buf[i] ^= 0xFF
920	            res = self.run_target(bytes(buf))
921	            cksum = hash_trace(classify_counts(res.trace))
922	            if cksum != entry.exec_cksum:
923	                eff_map[i] = True  # byte influences control flow
924	            self.save_if_interesting(bytes(buf), res, entry)
925	        if len(data) and not any(eff_map):
926	            eff_map = [True] * len(data)  # degenerate input: treat all as live
927	        return eff_map

933	        for i in range(len(data) - width + 1):

935	            for k in range(width):

1185	        choice = self._rand_below(rlim)
1186	        if choice == 0:

1229	        """Splice at a midpoint inside the region where the two seeds differ."""
1230	        if len(a) < 2 or len(b) < 2:
1231	            return None
1232	        n = min(len(a), len(b))

1234	        for i in range(n):

1238	                last_diff = i

1255	            if self.pending_favored:

1	"""AFLFast's Markov-chain bookkeeping and the AFLFast fuzzer itself.
2	
3	This module supplies the *state* half of AFLFast: the counters that the
4	power schedules in :mod:`fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules` consume.
5	
6	:class:`PathFrequencyTracker` implements the Markov chain of the paper.
7	A *state* is an execution path, identified -- exactly as AFL identifies a
8	"unique path" -- by the hash of the classified coverage trace.  For every
9	execution the tracker records
10	
11	* ``f(i)``: how many generated inputs exercised state ``i``,
12	* ``s(i)``: how many times a seed exercising state ``i`` was selected,
13	* ``T(i, j)``: how many times mutating a seed of state ``i`` produced an
14	  input of state ``j``, from which the transition probabilities
15	  ``P(i, j) = T(i, j) / sum_k T(i, k)`` are estimated.
16	
17	Rare paths (``f(i)`` far below the queue mean ``mu``) are flagged and given
18	an energy bonus, since they are the states from which undiscovered
19	neighbours are most likely reachable.
20	
21	:class:`AFLFastFuzzer` subclasses :class:`fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer.AFLFuzzer` and
22	changes exactly the two things AFLFast changes:
23	
24	1. ``power_schedule`` -- energy now comes from the selected
25	   :class:`~fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules.PowerSchedule` instead of being AFL's
26	   constant perf score;
27	2. seed selection order -- FAST/COE walk the queue in increasing ``s(i)``
28	   (:func:`prioritize_small_s`), the other schedules in increasing ``f(i)``
29	   (:func:`prioritize_small_f`).
30	
31	Everything else (bitmap, calibration, trimming, culling, deterministic /
32	havoc / splice stages) is inherited untouched.
33	
34	Determinism: all randomness still comes from the inherited
35	``numpy.random.RandomState`` seeded by the caller.
36	"""

83	        """Markov state id of a trace: the hash of its classified form."""
84	        return hash_trace(classify_counts(trace))
85	
86	    # -- recording --------------------------------------------------------
87	    def record_execution(self, state: str,
88	                         src_state: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
89	        """Count one input exercising ``state``, optionally as a transition.
90	
91	        ``src_state`` is the state of the seed the input was mutated from;
92	        passing it records the Markov transition ``src_state -> state``.
93	        """
94	        self.total_executions += 1
95	        if state not in self.freq:
96	            self.freq[state] = 0
97	            self.first_seen[state] = self.total_executions
98	            self.discovered_states += 1
99	        self.freq[state] += 1
100	        if src_state is not None:
101	            self.record_transition(src_state, state)
102	        return state
103	
104	    def observe(self, trace: Dict[int, int],
105	                src_state: Optional[str] = None) -> str:
106	        """Convenience wrapper: derive the state of ``trace`` and record it."""
107	        return self.record_execution(self.state_id(trace), src_state)
108	
109	    def record_transition(self, src: str, dst: str) -> None:
110	        """Count one Markov transition ``src -> dst``."""
111	        key = (src, dst)
112	        self.transitions[key] = self.transitions.get(key, 0) + 1
113	        self.out_degree[src] = self.out_degree.get(src, 0) + 1
114	
115	    def record_selection(self, state: str) -> int:
116	        """Count one selection of a seed exercising ``state`` (``s(i) += 1``)."""
117	        self.selections[state] = self.selections.get(state, 0) + 1
118	        return self.selections[state]
119	
120	    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
121	    def frequency(self, state: str) -> int:
122	        """``f(i)``: number of generated inputs that exercised ``state``."""
123	        return self.freq.get(state, 0)
124	
125	    def selection_count(self, state: str) -> int:
126	        """``s(i)``: number of times a seed of ``state`` has been selected."""
127	        return self.selections.get(state, 0)
128	
129	    def mu(self, states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> float:
130	        """``mu``: mean path frequency, over ``states`` or the whole chain."""
131	        keys = list(states) if states is not None else list(self.freq)
132	        if not keys:
133	            return 0.0
134	        return sum(self.frequency(k) for k in keys) / len(keys)
135	
136	    def relative_frequency(self, state: str,
137	                           states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> float:
138	        """``f(i) / mu`` -- the scale-free frequency the schedules consume."""
139	        mean = self.mu(states)
140	        if mean <= 0.0:
141	            return 0.0
142	        return self.frequency(state) / mean
143	
144	    def transition_probability(self, src: str, dst: str) -> float:
145	        """Maximum-likelihood estimate of ``P(src -> dst)``."""
146	        total = self.out_degree.get(src, 0)
147	        if total <= 0:
148	            return 0.0
149	        return self.transitions.get((src, dst), 0) / total
150	
151	    def transition_matrix(self) -> Dict[str, Dict[str, float]]:
152	        """Full estimated transition matrix ``P`` as nested dicts."""
153	        matrix: Dict[str, Dict[str, float]] = {}
154	        for (src, dst), count in self.transitions.items():
155	            total = self.out_degree.get(src, 0) or 1
156	            matrix.setdefault(src, {})[dst] = count / total
157	        return matrix
158	
159	    def self_transition_probability(self, state: str) -> float:
160	        """``P(i, i)``: how sticky a state is (AFLFast's core inefficiency)."""
161	        return self.transition_probability(state, state)
162	
163	    # -- rare paths -------------------------------------------------------
164	    def is_rare(self, state: str,
165	                states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> bool:
166	        """A path is rare when ``f(i) < rare_ratio * mu``."""
167	        return self.relative_frequency(state, states) < self.rare_ratio
168	
169	    def rare_states(self, states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> List[str]:
170	        """Every known state that currently counts as rare, sorted."""
171	        keys = list(states) if states is not None else sorted(self.freq)
172	        return [k for k in keys if self.is_rare(k, states)]
173	
174	    def rare_bonus(self, state: str,
175	                   states: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None) -> float:
176	        """Energy multiplier for ``state``: the bonus if rare, else 1."""
177	        return self.rare_bonus_factor if self.is_rare(state, states) else 1.0
178	
179	    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
180	        """Snapshot of the chain, for reports and tests."""
181	        return {
182	            "states": len(self.freq),
183	            "executions": self.total_executions,
184	            "transitions": len(self.transitions),
185	            "mu": self.mu(),
186	            "max_frequency": max(self.freq.values()) if self.freq else 0,
187	            "min_frequency": min(self.freq.values()) if self.freq else 0,
188	        }

195	def _entry_state(entry: QueueEntry) -> str:
196	    """Markov state of a queue entry (its calibration checksum)."""
197	    return entry.exec_cksum

199	
200	def prioritize_small_s(entries: Sequence[QueueEntry],
201	                       tracker: PathFrequencyTracker) -> List[QueueEntry]:
202	    """Order the queue by increasing ``s(i)`` -- used by FAST and COE.
203	
204	    Both schedules grow energy in ``s(i)``, so visiting the least-selected
205	    seeds first keeps the exponential from running away on one seed and
206	    gives every state at least one cheap visit before any state gets an
207	    expensive one.  Ties break on queue index, keeping the order stable.
208	    """
209	    return sorted(entries,
210	                  key=lambda e: (tracker.selection_count(_entry_state(e)),
211	                                 e.index))
212	
213	
214	def prioritize_small_f(entries: Sequence[QueueEntry],
215	                       tracker: PathFrequencyTracker) -> List[QueueEntry]:
216	    """Order the queue by increasing ``f(i)`` -- explore / linear / quad.
217	
218	    Those schedules do not grow with ``s(i)`` fast enough to escape a
219	    high-density region on their own, so the *ordering* carries the
220	    exploration pressure: least-exercised path first.  Ties break on queue
221	    index.
222	    """
223	    return sorted(entries,
224	                  key=lambda e: (tracker.frequency(_entry_state(e)), e.index))
225	
226	
227	def prioritize_queue_order(entries: Sequence[QueueEntry],
228	                           tracker: PathFrequencyTracker) -> List[QueueEntry]:
229	    """AFL's own FIFO order -- used by EXPLOIT, which is plain AFL."""
230	    return list(entries)

234	PRIORITIZERS = {
235	    PowerSchedule.EXPLOIT: prioritize_queue_order,
236	    PowerSchedule.EXPLORE: prioritize_small_f,
237	    PowerSchedule.COE: prioritize_small_s,
238	    PowerSchedule.FAST: prioritize_small_s,
239	    PowerSchedule.LINEAR: prioritize_small_f,
240	    PowerSchedule.QUAD: prioritize_small_f,
241	}

244	def prioritizer_for(schedule: PowerSchedule):
245	    """Return the prioritization function belonging to ``schedule``."""
246	    schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
247	    if schedule in S_PRIORITIZED_SCHEDULES:
248	        return prioritize_small_s
249	    return PRIORITIZERS[schedule]

256	class AFLFastFuzzer(AFLFuzzer):
257	    """AFL with an AFLFast power schedule and Markov-aware seed ordering."""
258	
259	    def __init__(self,
260	                 target: Any,
261	                 seeds: Sequence[bytes],
262	                 seed: int = 42,
263	                 dictionary: Optional[Sequence[bytes]] = None,
264	                 skip_deterministic: bool = False,
265	                 max_execs: int = 20000,
266	                 map_size: int = MAP_SIZE,
267	                 use_splicing: bool = True,
268	                 total_edges: Optional[int] = None,
269	                 schedule: PowerSchedule = PowerSchedule.FAST,
270	                 beta: float = POWER_BETA,
271	                 energy_cap: float = ENERGY_CAP_M,
272	                 rare_ratio: float = RARE_PATH_RATIO,
273	                 rare_bonus: float = RARE_PATH_BONUS,
274	                 use_prioritization: bool = True):
275	        self.schedule = PowerSchedule(schedule)
276	        self.tracker = PathFrequencyTracker(rare_ratio=rare_ratio,
277	                                            rare_bonus=rare_bonus)
278	        self.energy_computer = EnergyComputer(self.schedule, beta=beta,
279	                                              energy_cap=energy_cap,
280	                                              rare_ratio=rare_ratio,
281	                                              rare_bonus=rare_bonus)
282	        self.prioritize = prioritizer_for(self.schedule)
283	        self.use_prioritization = use_prioritization
284	
285	        # Bookkeeping for the experiment / reports.
286	        self.energy_log: List[float] = []
287	        self.energy_by_entry: Dict[int, List[float]] = {}
288	        self.cutoff_skips = 0
289	        self._cutoff_streak = 0
290	        self._current_state: Optional[str] = None
291	
292	        super().__init__(target=target, seeds=seeds, seed=seed,
293	                         dictionary=dictionary,
294	                         skip_deterministic=skip_deterministic,
295	                         max_execs=max_execs, map_size=map_size,
296	                         use_splicing=use_splicing, total_edges=total_edges)
297	
298	    # -- Markov bookkeeping ----------------------------------------------
299	    def run_target(self, data: bytes) -> ExecResult:
300	        """Run the target and fold the result into the Markov chain.
301	
302	        Every execution -- calibration, deterministic stage, havoc, splice
303	        or trim -- contributes to ``f(i)``, and every execution performed
304	        while fuzzing a seed also contributes the transition
305	        ``state(seed) -> state(mutant)``.
306	        """
307	        res = super().run_target(data)
308	        self.tracker.observe(res.trace, src_state=self._current_state)
309	        return res
310	
311	    def queue_states(self) -> List[str]:
312	        """Markov states currently represented in the queue."""
313	        return [_entry_state(e) for e in self.queue if e.exec_cksum]
314	
315	    def entry_inputs(self, entry: QueueEntry,
316	                     preview: bool = False) -> ScheduleInputs:
317	        """Bundle ``(alpha, f/mu, s)`` for ``entry`` for the schedule.
318	
319	        ``AFLFuzzer.calculate_score`` consumes one unit of ``handicap`` per
320	        call; ``preview=True`` restores it so that read-only reporting
321	        cannot perturb the campaign.
322	        """
323	        states = self.queue_states()
324	        state = _entry_state(entry)
325	        handicap = entry.handicap
326	        alpha = self.calculate_score(entry)
327	        if preview:
328	            entry.handicap = handicap
329	        return ScheduleInputs(
330	            alpha=alpha,
331	            freq=self.tracker.relative_frequency(state, states),
332	            sel=self.tracker.selection_count(state) or entry.n_fuzz,
333	        )
334	
335	    # -- energy -----------------------------------------------------------
336	    def power_schedule(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> float:
337	        """AFLFast energy: the selected schedule applied to ``(alpha, f, s)``.
338	
339	        ``alpha`` is AFL's own perf score, so AFLFast inherits AFL's speed /
340	        size / depth heuristics and only re-weights them by the Markov
341	        statistics.  The rare-path bonus is applied inside the
342	        :class:`~fuzzsim.aflfast_schedules.EnergyComputer`.
343	        """
344	        return self.energy_computer.energy_of(self.entry_inputs(entry))
345	
346	    def queue_inputs(self) -> List[ScheduleInputs]:
347	        """Read-only ``(alpha, f/mu, s)`` records for the whole queue."""
348	        return [self.entry_inputs(e, preview=True) for e in self.queue]
349	
350	    def schedule_energies(self) -> List[float]:
351	        """Energy the schedule would assign to each queue entry right now."""
352	        return self.energy_computer.compute_all(self.queue_inputs())
353	
354	    # -- seed selection ---------------------------------------------------
355	    def _skip_entry(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> bool:
356	        """AFL's favored-seed lottery, unchanged (see ``AFLFuzzer.select_next``)."""
357	        from fuzzsim.afl_fuzzer import (SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB, SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB,
358	                                        SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB)
359	        if self.pending_favored:
360	            return ((entry.was_fuzzed or not entry.favored)
361	                    and self._rand_below(100) < SKIP_TO_NEW_PROB)
362	        if not entry.favored and len(self.queue) > 10:
363	            if not entry.was_fuzzed:
364	                return self._rand_below(100) < SKIP_NFAV_NEW_PROB
365	            return self._rand_below(100) < SKIP_NFAV_OLD_PROB
366	        return False
367	
368	    def select_next(self, cursor: int) -> Tuple[Optional[QueueEntry], int]:
369	        """Walk the *prioritized* queue, keeping AFL's favored-skip lottery."""
370	        if not self.use_prioritization:
371	            return super().select_next(cursor)
372	        order = self.prioritize(self.queue, self.tracker)
373	        n = len(order)
374	        if n == 0:
375	            return None, 0
376	        for step in range(n):
377	            idx = (cursor + step) % n
378	            entry = order[idx]
379	            if self._skip_entry(entry):
380	                continue
381	            return entry, (idx + 1) % n
382	        return order[cursor % n], (cursor + 1) % n
383	
384	    # -- main loop --------------------------------------------------------
385	    def fuzz_one(self, entry: QueueEntry) -> int:
386	        """Fuzz one seed with the schedule's energy, honouring COE's cut-off."""
387	        entry.times_chosen += 1
388	        entry.n_fuzz += 1
389	        state = _entry_state(entry)
390	        self.tracker.record_selection(state)
391	        self._current_state = state
392	        try:
393	            energy = self.power_schedule(entry)
394	            entry.perf_score = energy
395	            self.energy_log.append(energy)
396	            self.energy_by_entry.setdefault(entry.index, []).append(energy)
397	
398	            # COE cut-off: an above-average path gets nothing at all.  The
399	            # streak guard stops the main loop spinning if the favored
400	            # lottery keeps handing us cut-off seeds.
401	            if energy <= 0.0 and self._cutoff_streak < MAX_CUTOFF_STREAK:
402	                self._cutoff_streak += 1
403	                self.cutoff_skips += 1
404	                return 0
405	            self._cutoff_streak = 0
406	
407	            if not entry.trim_done:
408	                self.trim_case(entry)
409	
410	            found = 0
411	            doing_det = not self.skip_deterministic and not entry.passed_det
412	            if doing_det:
413	                found += self.deterministic_stages(entry)
414	            found += self.havoc_stage(entry, energy, doing_det)
415	            found += self.splice_stage(entry, energy)
416	
417	            if not entry.was_fuzzed:
418	                entry.was_fuzzed = True
419	                self.pending_not_fuzzed = max(0, self.pending_not_fuzzed - 1)
420	                if entry.favored:
421	                    self.pending_favored = max(0, self.pending_favored - 1)
422	            entry.fuzz_count += 1
423	            return found
424	        finally:
425	            self._current_state = None
426	
427	    # -- reporting --------------------------------------------------------
428	    def stats(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
429	        stats = super().stats()
430	        specs = self.queue_inputs()
431	        stats.update({
432	            "schedule": self.schedule.value,
433	            "markov_states": len(self.tracker.freq),
434	            "markov_transitions": len(self.tracker.transitions),
435	            "mu": self.tracker.mu(self.queue_states()),
436	            "cutoff_skips": self.cutoff_skips,
437	            "energy_assignments": len(self.energy_log),
438	            "mean_assigned_energy": (sum(self.energy_log) / len(self.energy_log)
439	                                     if self.energy_log else 0.0),
440	            "queue_energies": self.energy_computer.compute_all(specs),
441	            "energy_summary": self.energy_computer.summary(specs),
442	            "rare_states": len(self.tracker.rare_states(self.queue_states())),
443	        })
444	        return stats
445	
446	    def path_frequencies(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
447	        """``f(i)`` for every queue state, keyed by state id."""
448	        return {s: self.tracker.frequency(s) for s in self.queue_states()}
449	
450	    def selection_counts(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
451	        """``s(i)`` for every queue state, keyed by state id."""
452	        return {s: self.tracker.selection_count(s) for s in self.queue_states()}
453	
454	    def covered_edge_set(self) -> Set[int]:
455	        return self.covered_edges()

1	"""FairFuzz mutation masking: influence detection and targeted havoc.
2	
3	Once a rare target branch has been chosen for a seed (see
4	:mod:`fuzzsim.fairfuzz_rare`), FairFuzz asks a second question: *which bytes
5	of the seed are responsible for reaching that branch?*  It answers it
6	empirically, by differential mutation:
7	
8	* For every byte position, replace the byte with a handful of random values
9	  and re-run the target.  If more than :data:`INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD` of those
10	  probes destroy the target branch hit, the position is **influential** and
11	  must be preserved; otherwise it is **safe** to mutate.
12	* The result is a :class:`MutationMask`; masks are memoised by
13	  ``(sha1(data), target_branch)`` because the same seed is re-targeted on
14	  every queue cycle and probing is the expensive part.
15	* :class:`MaskedHavocMutator` then runs AFL's havoc operators restricted to
16	  the safe positions.  Crucially it never *shifts* the influential bytes:
17	  length-changing operators are confined to the tail region past the last
18	  influential position, everything else is in-place.
19	
20	:class:`FairFuzzFuzzer` glues the two halves onto the AFL core: for each
21	queue entry it picks a rare branch the entry hits, computes the mask and
22	replaces AFL's havoc stage with the targeted variant.
23	
24	Determinism: every random draw comes from a ``numpy.random.RandomState``
25	seeded from an explicit seed (42 in the experiments).
26	"""
27

53	# Configuration constants
54	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
55	
56	#: Random replacements tried per byte position when probing for influence.
57	NUM_PROBES = 8
58	
59	#: A position is influential when strictly more than 60% of its probes
60	#: destroy the target branch hit (FairFuzz's statistical criterion).
61	INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD = 0.6
62	
63	#: Longest prefix of an input that is probed (probing costs one exec per
64	#: probe per position, so very long inputs are only partially masked).
65	MAX_MASK_LEN = 256

68	@dataclass
69	class MutationMask:
70	    """Which byte positions of an input may be mutated freely.
71	
72	    ``influential`` holds the positions that must keep their value (and their
73	    offset) for the target branch to stay hit; every other position below
74	    ``length`` is safe.
75	    """
76	
77	    length: int
78	    influential: Set[int] = field(default_factory=set)
79	    scores: Dict[int, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
80	    target_branch: Optional[int] = None
81	    probes_used: int = 0
82	    hits_target: bool = True
83	
84	    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
85	    def is_safe(self, pos: int) -> bool:
86	        return 0 <= pos < self.length and pos not in self.influential
87	
88	    def is_influential(self, pos: int) -> bool:
89	        return pos in self.influential
90	
91	    def safe_positions(self) -> List[int]:
92	        return [i for i in range(self.length) if i not in self.influential]
93	
94	    def span_is_safe(self, pos: int, width: int) -> bool:
95	        """True when a whole ``width``-byte write at ``pos`` stays on safe bytes."""
96	        if pos < 0 or pos + width > self.length:
97	            return False
98	        return all(i not in self.influential for i in range(pos, pos + width))
99	
100	    def safe_runs(self) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
101	        """Maximal ``(start, length)`` runs of consecutive safe positions."""
102	        runs: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
103	        start: Optional[int] = None
104	        for i in range(self.length + 1):
105	            safe = i < self.length and i not in self.influential
106	            if safe and start is None:
107	                start = i
108	            elif not safe and start is not None:
109	                runs.append((start, i - start))
110	                start = None
111	        return runs
112	
113	    def tail_start(self) -> int:
114	        """First offset after the last influential byte.
115	
116	        Inserting or deleting at or after this offset cannot shift any
117	        influential byte, so length-changing operators are allowed there.
118	        """
119	        return (max(self.influential) + 1) if self.influential else 0
120	
121	    @property
122	    def n_influential(self) -> int:
123	        return len(self.influential)
124	
125	    @property
126	    def n_safe(self) -> int:
127	        return max(0, self.length - len(self.influential))
128	
129	    @property
130	    def safe_ratio(self) -> float:
131	        return (self.n_safe / self.length) if self.length else 1.0
132	
133	    def __len__(self) -> int:
134	        return self.length
135	
136	    # -- construction -----------------------------------------------------
137	    @classmethod
138	    def from_scores(cls, length: int, scores: Dict[int, float],
139	                    threshold: float = INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD,
140	                    target_branch: Optional[int] = None,
141	                    probes_used: int = 0,
142	                    hits_target: bool = True) -> "MutationMask":
143	        """Build a mask from per-position 'fraction of probes destroyed'."""
144	        influential = {pos for pos, frac in scores.items() if frac > threshold}
145	        return cls(length=length, influential=influential, scores=dict(scores),
146	                   target_branch=target_branch, probes_used=probes_used,
147	                   hits_target=hits_target)
148	
149	    @classmethod
150	    def all_safe(cls, length: int,
151	                 target_branch: Optional[int] = None,
152	                 hits_target: bool = True) -> "MutationMask":
153	        return cls(length=length, influential=set(), target_branch=target_branch,
154	                   hits_target=hits_target)

157	class InfluenceDetector:
158	    """Probe-based (differential mutation) detector of influential bytes.
159	
160	    ``runner`` is any callable mapping ``bytes`` to the set of branch ids the
161	    target executes.  Every ``detect`` call is memoised on the hash of the
162	    input plus the target branch, so repeated queue cycles over the same seed
163	    are free.
164	    """
165	
166	    def __init__(self,
167	                 runner: Callable[[bytes], Set[int]],
168	                 rng: Optional[np.random.RandomState] = None,
169	                 probes: int = NUM_PROBES,
170	                 threshold: float = INFLUENCE_THRESHOLD,
171	                 fast: bool = True,
172	                 max_len: int = MAX_MASK_LEN,
173	                 seed: int = 42):
174	        self.runner = runner
175	        self.rng = rng if rng is not None else np.random.RandomState(seed)
176	        self.probes = int(probes)
177	        self.threshold = float(threshold)
178	        self.fast = bool(fast)
179	        self.max_len = int(max_len)
180	
181	        self.cache: Dict[Tuple[str, int], MutationMask] = {}
182	        self.cache_hits = 0
183	        self.cache_misses = 0
184	        self.probe_execs = 0
185	
186	    # -- cache ------------------------------------------------------------
187	    @staticmethod
188	    def data_hash(data: bytes) -> str:
189	        """Stable content hash used as the first half of the cache key."""
190	        return hashlib.sha1(bytes(data)).hexdigest()[:16]
191	
192	    def cache_key(self, data: bytes, target_branch: int) -> Tuple[str, int]:
193	        return (self.data_hash(data), int(target_branch))
194	
195	    def clear_cache(self) -> None:
196	        self.cache.clear()
197	
198	    def cache_stats(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
199	        return {"size": len(self.cache), "hits": self.cache_hits,
200	                "misses": self.cache_misses, "probe_execs": self.probe_execs}
201	
202	    # -- probing ----------------------------------------------------------
203	    def _random_replacement(self, orig: int) -> int:
204	        """A random byte value different from the original one."""
205	        return (orig + 1 + int(self.rng.randint(0, 255))) & 0xFF
206	
207	    def probe_position(self, data: bytes, pos: int, target_branch: int,
208	                       fast: Optional[bool] = None) -> float:
209	        """Fraction of random replacements at ``pos`` that lose the branch.
210	
211	        With the fast variant the loop stops as soon as the verdict can no
212	        longer change: once more than ``threshold`` of the total probes have
213	        destroyed the hit (influential), or once even destroying every
214	        remaining probe could not reach the threshold (safe).
215	        """
216	        use_fast = self.fast if fast is None else fast
217	        buf = bytearray(data)
218	        orig = buf[pos]
219	        destroyed = 0
220	        needed = self.threshold * self.probes  # strictly-greater comparison
221	        for i in range(self.probes):
222	            buf[pos] = self._random_replacement(orig)
223	            edges = self.runner(bytes(buf))
224	            self.probe_execs += 1
225	            if target_branch not in edges:
226	                destroyed += 1
227	            if use_fast:
228	                remaining = self.probes - i - 1
229	                if destroyed > needed:  # already influential
230	                    return (destroyed + remaining) / self.probes
231	                if destroyed + remaining <= needed:  # can no longer qualify
232	                    return destroyed / self.probes
233	        buf[pos] = orig
234	        return destroyed / self.probes
